# gh-1605: FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

## Problem
FinalizeGate verifies the produced state from the agent's own shell — same cwd, same env, same session state. The TB-2.1 verifier instead runs the entry points itself, typically via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, script])` from a different working directory with a fresh environment. A deliverable that depends on cwd/env passes the agent's self-check and fails the grader, and the agent never notices.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-8/modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a/agent/fa.txt` (final ledger): `actual: "Station 101 mean temperature: -15.5°C / Station 102 mean temperature: 30.3°C" ... status: pass` for every checklist item, `__FA_EXIT=0`.
- Same trial, `verifier/test-stdout.txt`: `AssertionError: Station 102 mean should be 30.3°C, got 15.5` — under the verifier's subprocess the script produced different output (Station 102 collapsed to station 101's value), i.e., behavior diverged between the agent's `cd /app && python3 ...` run and the verifier's clean run. Reward 0.0 on a task where 4/5 sibling trials passed.

## Proposed fix
- Add a FinalizeGate named check: "grader parity" — re-run each produced entry point the way a grader would: `cd /` (or another neutral cwd distinct from the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars), `subprocess`-style invocation, capture stdout/stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run.
- Flag any divergence (different output, missing files created by relative paths, locale/encoding-dependent output) as a `fail` item in the ledger instead of pass.
- Document the check in the FinalizeGate checklist so the model performs it before finalizing.

## Acceptance
1. REG/eval test: a script whose output differs between `/app` and `/` cwd is caught (ledger shows `fail`), not passed.
2. The modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a replay ends with the divergence detected before finalize.
3. No false positives for cwd-independent scripts (parity run matches in-session run → pass).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

name: finalize_gate
description: The FinalizeGate completion contract (gh-1412) — unattended/bench mode only; the agent re-verifies produced state against the task text with real commands before declaring done, and ends the final answer with a task-ledger block.
---
## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.

# gh-1605: FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

## Problem
FinalizeGate verifies the produced state from the agent's own shell — same cwd, same env, same session state. The TB-2.1 verifier instead runs the entry points itself, typically via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, script])` from a different working directory with a fresh environment. A deliverable that depends on cwd/env passes the agent's self-check and fails the grader, and the agent never notices.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-8/modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a/agent/fa.txt` (final ledger): `actual: "Station 101 mean temperature: -15.5°C / Station 102 mean temperature: 30.3°C" ... status: pass` for every checklist item, `__FA_EXIT=0`.
- Same trial, `verifier/test-stdout.txt`: `AssertionError: Station 102 mean should be 30.3°C, got 15.5` — under the verifier's subprocess the script produced different output (Station 102 collapsed to station 101's value), i.e., behavior diverged between the agent's `cd /app && python3 ...` run and the verifier's clean run. Reward 0.0 on a task where 4/5 sibling trials passed.

## Proposed fix
- Add a FinalizeGate named check: "grader parity" — re-run each produced entry point the way a grader would: `cd /` (or another neutral cwd distinct from the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars), `subprocess`-style invocation, capture stdout/stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run.
- Flag any divergence (different output, missing files created by relative paths, locale/encoding-dependent output) as a `fail` item in the ledger instead of pass.
- Document the check in the FinalizeGate checklist so the model performs it before finalizing.

## Acceptance
1. REG/eval test: a script whose output differs between `/app` and `/` cwd is caught (ledger shows `fail`), not passed.
2. The modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a replay ends with the divergence detected before finalize.
3. No false positives for cwd-independent scripts (parity run matches in-session run → pass).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).

  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.

---
name: finalize_gate
description: The FinalizeGate completion contract (gh-1412) — unattended/bench mode only; the agent re-verifies produced state against the task text with real commands before declaring done, and ends the final answer with a task-ledger block.
---
## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.

Hosts inject `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms; resolved live per turn through the session-correlation seam above, so a mid-session `/timer` change reaches the next bash exec and the next LLM request); `fa --timer 25m` / `--deadline <duration|epoch>` (headless AND interactive) and the TUI `/timer` slash-command write the same single session value (env < flag < `/timer`; later wins). While armed, every LLM request context carries a per-turn `time-left: …` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at the ladder crossings (~50%, the T-3min wrap-up/background-job-drain steer, T-30s); the TUI status line renders a countdown chip as a pure projection. Missing/invalid env = feature off, byte-for-byte today's behavior; an explicit invalid user spec is a clear `FormatException`, never a silent wrong clock. Pure Dart — the clock is injected, no `dart:io` in `lib/`.

Now I understand the loop machinery. The FinalizeGate is: prompt contract + ledger parsing/stripping + event. There is no mechanical execution of checks — the MODEL runs checks via bash, and the ledger records them.

For gh-1605, the "proposed fix" says: add a named check "grader parity" to the checklist; document it so the model performs it. The acceptance criteria:

1. REG/eval test: a script whose output differs between `/app` and `/` cwd is caught (ledger shows `fail`), not passed.
2. Replay of the evidence trial ends with divergence detected before finalize.
3. No false positives for cwd-independent scripts (parity run matches → pass).

Given this repo's architecture, here's my plan:

### 1. Prompt change (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`)
Add a named check bullet:

- **Grader parity** — before declaring pass on any produced entry point (script/CLI/command the grader will run), re-run it the way the verifier will: a different working directory (e.g. `cd /` or any cwd distinct from the session's), a clean environment (`env -i <abs-path-to-interpreter> <entry-point>` or `subprocess`-style fresh process with no session-exported vars), and capture stdout/stderr + exit code. Diff against the earlier in-session run — any divergence (different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output) is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass. Graders run from THEIR cwd, never yours.

Wording should be concise, follow style of other bullets.

### 2. Regenerate prompts.g.dart
`dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart`.

### 3. Tests

**(a) UT** in `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` (or maybe there's a prompts test file) asserting the prompt contains the grader-parity named check (e.g. `contains('Grader parity')`).

**(b) REG/eval test (acceptance 1)**: integration-style test with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash:
- Fixture: create `/app`-like dir containing a script whose output depends on cwd (e.g. reads a data file via relative path... wait, need output to DIFFER between /app and / cwd runs; e.g. script reads `data.txt` in cwd if present else a default, or uses `pwd`? Something realistic: a script computing stats from `stations.csv` found via relative path `./stations.csv`, falling back to a wrong bundled default → from /app it reads the right file; from / it reads a stale file in / or produces the fallback).

Then the scripted agent: turn 1 — run the script in-session (in the fixture dir) → output A; turn 2 — run the parity check the way the prompt prescribes: `cd / && <abs path> script` → output B ≠ A; turn 3 — final answer with ledger containing the parity item marked `fail` (divergence detected before finalize). Assert:
- The persisted `task_ledger` record exists and its parity item status is `fail` (acceptance 1: "ledger shows fail, not passed").
- The run's final answer (stripped) does NOT claim success on the parity item... (the strip happens anyway).

**(c) acceptance 3**: mirrored test where the script is cwd-independent: parity run matches in-session run → ledger shows `pass` (no false positive). This is again model-scripted... the "no false positives" criterion in a scripted test means: when outputs match, the scripted ledger item is pass and the record verifies allVerified. Hmm, this is somewhat tautological since the model decides. But as a REG eval harness test, what it pins is: the REAL bash execution of the parity commands produces matching output for a cwd-independent script (i.e., the fixture + the prescribed check command shape do not spuriously diverge), and the ledger's `pass` item survives parsing with `verified == true`.

Alternatively, a **deterministic unit test** of the parity mechanics: a Dart test that runs the parity procedure itself (via `Process.run` / `LocalShell`) against two fixture scripts — one cwd-dependent, one cwd-independent — and asserts divergence detected / match detected. That's a real, non-tautological REG test: it pins that the RECOMMENDED parity procedure actually catches the failure mode (acceptance 1) and doesn't false-positive (acceptance 3). That is the substance of the named check: if the recommended command shape (clean env + neutral cwd + fresh subprocess) didn't actually catch cwd-dependent scripts, the check would be worthless.

Where to put such a test? There's `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` (unit) and `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` (integration, tagged `integration`, uses real processes). The parity procedure test uses real processes (Process.run with workingDirectory + clean environment) — that's fine for a unit test on the VM actually (`dart:io` Process.run directly in test/ is fine; integration tag is for the full CLI boot). Let me check how existing tests use Process.run directly. E.g. tests for LocalShell. Let me look at the test tree structure.

Also check: maybe there's an existing "checklist"/"named checks" concept in code I should extend (like a structured list of named checks the loop validates?). Let me grep "Executable bit" in test/ to see how prompt tests cover the named checks.

Plan (TDD where it makes sense — the guideline mandates TDD; for a prompt-text change, the "test first" is the prompt content test):

1. **RED**: Add tests:
   - In `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart`: extend the "enumerates the named checklist items" test (or add a new test) asserting the contract carries the **Grader parity** check with its key phrases: e.g. `contains('Grader parity')`, `contains('clean env')` / 'fresh subprocess' / 'different working directory'. 
   - A new REG test — the parity procedure itself. Where? A new file `test/agent/finalize_gate_parity_test.dart`? It uses real `Process.run` — fine on VM. Actually let me think about what this test does:
     - Fixture 1 (cwd-dependent, the modernize-scientific-stack failure shape): a python script that reads a data file by RELATIVE path from cwd, with a fallback default → running from the data dir gives "Station 101: -15.5 / Station 102: 30.3", running from `/` gives the fallback ("Station 102 collapsed to 101's value" shape). Assert: in-session run (cwd=fixture dir) output ≠ parity run (cwd='/') output → divergence detected → the ledger item the prompt mandates for this case is `fail`.
     - Fixture 2 (cwd-independent): a script whose output is the same from any cwd. Assert parity run output == in-session run output → `pass`.
     
     But hold on — in the repo's architecture, WHO decides fail/pass? The model. So a pure-Dart test asserting "divergence detected" is really testing: THE PRESCRIBED PROCEDURE detects divergence. That's exactly what acceptance 1 asks ("a script whose output differs between /app and / cwd is caught") and acceptance 3 ("no false positives for cwd-independent scripts"). The test can also shape the result as a `TaskLedgerItem` and assert `status: fail`/`pass` + `verified` semantics — tying it to the ledger vocabulary. That's a fair REG test: it pins the check's mechanics so future changes to the recommended procedure don't silently break it.

     Where do I get python3? Not guaranteed on all runners... The evidence trial is python-based, but the test should be hermetic. Better: use `dart` scripts? `dart run` is slow. Use SHELL scripts (bash) — the agent sessions run bash; the grader uses `subprocess.run([sys.executable, script])` but for the REG test any interpreter works. A bash script whose output depends on cwd:
     ```bash
     #!/usr/bin/env bash
     if [[ -f ./stations.csv ]]; then ... else echo fallback; fi
     ```
     That's cwd-dependent via relative path. And exit codes/encoding can be tested too. Bash is guaranteed on the linux CI. But to mirror the grader parity shape (absolute interpreter path, no session env), use `Process.run('/bin/bash', [absScriptPath], workingDirectory: '/', environment: <string, string>{})`... environment: pure clean env may break bash (PATH needed) — use `environment: {'PATH': ...}`? A "clean env" in the test can be a minimal env: `{'PATH': Platform.environment['PATH']}`. Actually for the parity test to be realistic, env cleanness matters for the env-divergence axis (session-exported vars). I can include a third fixture: script whose output depends on an env var the "session" exported (`export STATION_FALLBACK=...`), demonstrating clean-env parity catches env leakage too. # gh-1605: FinalizeGate: verify deliverables the way the verifier will (fresh cwd/env, subprocess parity) before declaring pass

## Description

## Problem
FinalizeGate verifies the produced state from the agent's own shell — same cwd, same env, same session state. The TB-2.1 verifier instead runs the entry points itself, typically via `subprocess.run([sys.executable, script])` from a different working directory with a fresh environment. A deliverable that depends on cwd/env passes the agent's self-check and fails the grader, and the agent never notices.

## Evidence
- `fa-2.1-docker-cpu-8/modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a/agent/fa.txt` (final ledger): `actual: "Station 101 mean temperature: -15.5°C / Station 102 mean temperature: 30.3°C" ... status: pass` for every checklist item, `__FA_EXIT=0`.
- Same trial, `verifier/test-stdout.txt`: `AssertionError: Station 102 mean should be 30.3°C, got 15.5` — under the verifier's subprocess the script produced different output (Station 102 collapsed to station 101's value), i.e., behavior diverged between the agent's `cd /app && python3 ...` run and the verifier's clean run. Reward 0.0 on a task where 4/5 sibling trials passed.

## Proposed fix
- Add a FinalizeGate named check: "grader parity" — re-run each produced entry point the way a grader would: `cd /` (or another neutral cwd distinct from the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars), `subprocess`-style invocation, capture stdout/stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run.
- Flag any divergence (different output, missing files created by relative paths, locale/encoding-dependent output) as a `fail` item in the ledger instead of pass.
- Document the check in the FinalizeGate checklist so the model performs it before finalizing.

## Acceptance
1. REG/eval test: a script whose output differs between `/app` and `/` cwd is caught (ledger shows `fail`), not passed.
2. The modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a replay ends with the divergence detected before finalize.
3. No false positives for cwd-independent scripts (parity run matches in-session run → pass).

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).

---
name: finalize_gate
description: The FinalizeGate completion contract (gh-1412) — unattended/bench mode only; the agent re-verifies produced state against the task text with real commands before declaring done, and ends the final answer with a task-ledger block.
---
## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.';

Hosts inject `FA_DEADLINE_EPOCH_MS` (epoch ms; resolved live per turn through the session-correlation seam above, so a mid-session `/timer` change reaches the next bash exec and the next LLM request); `fa --timer 25m` / `--deadline <duration|epoch>` (headless AND interactive) and the TUI `/timer` slash-command write the same single session value (env < flag < `/timer`; later wins). While armed, every LLM request context carries a per-turn `time-left: …` line and one-shot `<system-notice>` steerings fire at the ladder crossings (~50%, the T-3min wrap-up/background-job-drain steer, T-30s); the TUI status line renders a countdown chip as a pure projection. Missing/invalid env = feature off, byte-for-byte today's behavior; an explicit invalid user spec is a clear `FormatException`, never a silent wrong clock. Pure Dart — the clock is injected, no `dart:io` in `lib/`.

Now I understand the loop machinery. The FinalizeGate is: prompt contract + ledger parsing/stripping + event. There is no mechanical execution of checks — the MODEL runs checks via bash, and the ledger records them.

For gh-1605, the "proposed fix" says: add a named check "grader parity" to the checklist; document it so the model performs it. The acceptance criteria:

1. REG/eval test: a script whose output differs between `/app` and `/` cwd is caught (ledger shows `fail`), not passed.
2. Replay of the evidence trial ends with divergence detected before finalize.
3. No false positives for cwd-independent scripts (parity run matches → pass).

Given this repo's architecture, here's my plan:

### 1. Prompt change (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`)
Add a named check bullet:

- **Grader parity** — before declaring pass on any produced entry point (script/CLI/command the grader will run), re-run it the way the verifier will: a different working directory (e.g. `cd /` or any cwd distinct from the session's), a clean environment (`env -i <abs-path-to-interpreter> <entry-point>` or `subprocess`-style fresh process with no session-exported vars), and capture stdout/stderr + exit code. Diff against the earlier in-session run — any divergence (different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output) is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass. Graders run from THEIR cwd, never yours.

Wording should be concise, follow style of other bullets.

### 2. Regenerate prompts.g.dart
`dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart`.

### 3. Tests

**(a) UT** in `test/cli/finalize_gate_prompt_test.dart` (or maybe there's a prompts test file) asserting the prompt contains the grader-parity named check (e.g. `contains('Grader parity')`).

**(b) REG/eval test (acceptance 1)**: integration-style test with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash:
- Fixture: create `/app`-like dir containing a script whose output depends on cwd (e.g. reads a data file via relative path... wait, need output to DIFFER between /app and / cwd runs; e.g. script reads `data.txt` in cwd if present else a default, or uses `pwd`? Something realistic: a script computing stats from `stations.csv` found via relative path `./stations.csv`, falling back to a wrong bundled default → from /app it reads the right file; from / it reads a stale file in / or produces the fallback).

Then the scripted agent: turn 1 — run the script in-session (in the fixture dir) → output A; turn 2 — run the parity check the way the prompt prescribes: `cd / && <abs path> script` → output B ≠ A; turn 3 — final answer with ledger containing the parity item marked `fail` (divergence detected before finalize). Assert:
- The persisted `task_ledger` record exists and its parity item status is `fail` (acceptance 1: "ledger shows fail, not passed").
- The run's final answer (stripped) does NOT claim success on the parity item... (the strip happens anyway).

**(c) acceptance 3**: mirrored test where the script is cwd-independent: parity run matches in-session run → ledger shows `pass` (no false positive). This is again model-scripted... the "no false positives" criterion in a scripted test means: when outputs match, the scripted ledger item is pass and the record verifies allVerified. Hmm, this is somewhat tautological since the model decides. But as a REG eval harness test, what it pins is: the REAL bash execution of the parity commands produces matching output for a cwd-independent script (i.e., the fixture + the prescribed check command shape do not spuriously diverge), and the ledger's `pass` item survives parsing with `verified == true`.

Alternatively, a **deterministic unit test** of the parity mechanics: a Dart test that runs the parity procedure itself (via `Process.run` / `LocalShell`) against two fixture scripts — one cwd-dependent, one cwd-independent — and asserts divergence detected / match detected. That's a real, non-tautological REG test: it pins that the RECOMMENDED parity procedure actually catches the failure mode (acceptance 1) and doesn't false-positive (acceptance 3). That is the substance of the named check: if the recommended command shape (clean env + neutral cwd + fresh subprocess) didn't actually catch cwd-dependent scripts, the check would be worthless.

Where to put such a test? There's `test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart` (unit) and `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` (integration, tagged `integration`, uses real processes). The parity procedure test uses real processes (Process.run with workingDirectory + clean environment) — that's fine for a unit test on the VM actually (`dart:io` Process.run directly in test/ is fine; integration tag is for the full CLI boot). Let me check how existing tests use Process.run directly. E.g. tests for LocalShell. Let me look at the test tree structure.

Also check: maybe there's an existing "checklist"/"named checks" concept in code I should extend (like a structured list of named checks the loop validates?). Let me grep "Executable bit" in test/ to see how prompt tests cover the named checks.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

---
name: finalize_gate
description: The FinalizeGate completion contract (gh-1412) — unattended/bench mode only; the agent re-verifies produced state against the task text with real commands before declaring done, and ends the final answer with a task-ledger block.
---
## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:127:    '## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.';

---
name: finalize_gate
description: The FinalizeGate completion contract (gh-1412) — unattended/bench mode only; the agent re-verifies produced state against the task text with real commands before declaring done, and ends the final answer with a task-ledger block.
---
## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:127:    '## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.';

---
name: finalize_gate
description: The FinalizeGate completion contract (gh-1412) — unattended/bench mode only; the agent re-verifies produced state against the task text with real commands before declaring done, and ends the final answer with a task-ledger block.
---
## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:127:    '## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.';

---
name: finalize_gate
description: The FinalizeGate completion contract (gh-1412) — unattended/bench mode only; the agent re-verifies produced state against the task text with real commands before declaring done, and ends the final answer with a task-ledger block.
---
## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.

lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart:127:    '## FinalizeGate — verify produced state before declaring done

You are running unattended: nobody re-checks your work after you declare it. **Trivial turns — answer directly:** when the turn made NO tool calls at all — no files written or edited, no commands run, nothing created or changed; a pure question answered from what you already know — there is nothing to verify. Skip the checklist AND the task ledger entirely and reply plainly; the gate exists for produced state, and with none the checklist is noise.

The contract does NOT apply to turns like:

- **"почему ты баш команды вызываешь?"** — a "why did you…" question. Just answer it directly: no checklist, no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what does the `read` selector `:N` do?"** — a "what does X do" question. Just explain it: no verification commands, no ledger.
- **"what's the status?"** — a status/explanation answer about work already done. Report it plainly: no re-verification, no ledger.

Those turns produced no state; running the checklist ritual on them is noise. Otherwise, before ANY final summary you MUST:

1. **Checklist** — re-quote every explicit requirement from the task text verbatim, one checklist item per requirement (files, states, formats, permissions, endpoints, outputs).
2. **Verify each item with a real command** against the produced state — never from memory, never "I wrote it earlier". Note expected vs actual.
3. **Fix or report every unmet item** — a failed item is either fixed and re-verified, or explicitly reported as unmet. Fix attempts are bounded: report, don't spiral.

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

```task-ledger
- requirement: <verbatim requirement quote>
  command: <the verification command you ran>
  expected: <what it should show>
  actual: <what it actually showed>
  status: pass|fixed|fail
```

`pass` = verified against the produced state; `fixed` = failed, then fixed and re-verified; `fail` = could not meet it, reported. A final answer whose ledger still has `fail` items without an explicit report is a protocol violation.';
