arguments.content:
### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

{"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).
- **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: a produced entry point (a script/CLI the grader will run) is verified only when it survives the grader's own invocation. Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass.

{"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).
- **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: a produced entry point (a script/CLI the grader will run) is verified only when it survives the grader's own invocation. Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass.

{"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

{"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.

Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. {"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).
- **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: a produced entry point (a script/CLI the grader will run) is verified only when it survives the grader's own invocation. Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass.

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

{"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).

Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. {"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

{"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.

Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. {"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).
- **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: a produced entry point (a script/CLI the grader will run) is verified only when it survives the grader's own invocation. Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass.

End the final answer with the task ledger — a fenced `task-ledger` block, one entry per checklist item:

{"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).

- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).
- **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: a produced entry point (a script/CLI the grader will run) is verified only when it survives the grader's own invocation. Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass.

{"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. {"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>

blocks.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print the test dirs/files of one shard from scripts/test_shards.json.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/shard_files.py <manifest> <index> [--exclude STR]...

Output: one path per line, suitable for
    dart test $(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_shards.json 0)

Directory units are printed as-is (dart test accepts directories). The
special unit "test" (loose *_test.dart files at the test root) is expanded
to the individual root-level files so that `dart test` does not run the
entire suite. File-level manifests (every *_test.dart is a unit — e.g.
packages/fa_ui, issue #283) print their units directly.

Top-level test dirs that exist on disk but are MISSING from the manifest
(a PR added one after the last weekly rebalance) are bin-packed across the
shards at runtime by file count, so new suites run this PR — not at some
future rebalance (issue #194, AC5). For file-level manifests the same
runtime bin-pack applies per uncovered FILE (issue #283, E2).
test/integration is excluded from the core shards: issue #551 gives it a
dedicated per-PR gate stage (no-key legs) plus the tag-only provider smoke.
--exclude STR
drops paths containing STR (e.g. golden — host-locked suites stay out of
the shards even when a PR adds one post-rebalance, issue #283 E4).
--exclude-tag TAG (gh-1199 AC1, tag-boundary manifests)
drops every FILE whose real (non-comment) @Tags annotation names TAG —
the deterministic-gate integration shards pass --exclude-tag llm so no
live-provider file is ever selected for the merge-blocking gate, however
it reached the manifest (rebalance inclusion or runtime bin-pack). Only
file-level manifest units are tag-checked; directory units pass through
(the dart-test invocation's --exclude-tags is the backstop there).
--tags TAG (issue #931, integration shards)
inverts the integration exclusion: only files whose @Tags annotation names
TAG are bin-packed as uncovered, so an INTEGRATION manifest (e.g.
scripts/test_integration_shards.json) auto-runs a PR's new integration
tests — and never swallows untagged core files.

Pure stdlib.
"""

import glob
import json
import os
import re
import sys


def uncovered_units(covered: set, root: str) -> list:
    """Top-level test dirs missing from the manifest, as (path, filecount)."""
    out = []
    for entry in sorted(os.listdir(root)):
        path = os.path.join(root, entry)
        if entry == "integration" or path in covered or not os.path.isdir(path):
            continue  # integration runs in its own CI job
        files = glob.glob(os.path.join(path, "**", "*_test.dart"), recursive=True)
        if files:
            out.append((path.replace(os.sep, "/"), len(files)))
    return out

Named checks every checklist must include when they apply:

- **Executable bit + shebang** on every script or binary you created (`test -x path`, shebang present) — a working file without +x is a failed task.
- **Final state** — after any destructive self-test, restore the state the task's canonical flow ends in (the repo/service the task describes, its post-test state included).
- **Canonical artifacts** — verify with the artifacts the task PROVIDES (configs, datasets, archives, URLs), never a self-made stand-in.
- **Credential hunt** — before declaring "no credentials": enumerate the standard places with real commands (environment, `~/.aws/`, `~/.config/`, `~/.hf/`, `~/.git-credentials`, `~/[REDACTED:Credential File]`, instance metadata when available, the task directory and its dotfiles). A declined `request_secret` in an unattended run means "hunt harder", not "give up".
- **Content, not existence** — a file or endpoint existing is not the requirement; its CONTENT matching the task is (cat the file, curl the page, diff the format, run the command the task says must succeed).
- **Grader parity** — your shell is not the verifier's: a produced entry point (a script/CLI the grader will run) is verified only when it survives the grader's own invocation. Re-run each produced entry point from a different working directory (`cd /` — any neutral cwd, never the session cwd) in a fresh subprocess with a clean env (no session-exported vars), capture stdout, stderr and exit code, and diff against the earlier in-session run. Any divergence — different output, files created via relative paths now missing, locale/encoding-dependent output — is a `fail` ledger item, not a pass.

{"content":"### What changed

Added a **Grader parity** named check to the FinalizeGate contract (`prompts/cli/finalize_gate.md`, compiled into the system prompt via `gen_prompts`): before finalizing, every produced entry point is re-run the way the verifier will run it — fresh subprocess, neutral cwd (never the session cwd), clean env (no session-exported vars) — and stdout/stderr/exit code are diffed against the in-session run. Any divergence is a `fail` ledger item, never a pass.

### Key decisions

- Prompt-level check (like the existing executable-bit / canonical-artifacts checks), not a new engine mechanism — the agent already verifies via bash; the contract now pins the grader's invocation shape.
- The parity rule is regression-proven, not just documented: `test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart` replays the modernize-scientific-stack__nwbgy7a failure shape (a script resolving its dataset via the CWD: in-session run prints `Station 102: 30.3`, clean-cwd run silently falls back to `15.5`) and asserts the parity item lands as `fail` through the real `formatTaskLedgerBlock`/`parseTaskLedger` pipeline; a cwd/env-independent entry point parity-passes (no false positive, `allVerified` green).
- IT-3 in `test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart` replays the trial end-to-end with the scripted mock-LLM + real bash: the divergence is detected and persisted as a `fail` `task_ledger` record before the run finalizes.

### How to verify

```bash
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_grader_parity_test.dart
dart test test/agent/finalize_gate_test.dart   # prompt-content UT (gh-1605)
dart test --tags integration test/integration/fa_finalize_gate_test.dart
```

<details><summary>Parity check flow</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  EP[Produced entry point] --> INS["In-session run (session cwd + env)"]
  EP --> PAR["Grader-parity run: fresh subprocess, neutral cwd, clean env"]
  INS --> DIFF{stdout / stderr / exit code equal?}
  PAR --> DIFF
  DIFF -->|yes| PASS["ledger item: pass"]
  DIFF -->|no| FAIL["ledger item: fail — never a silent pass"]
```

</details>
